panels.title: Decode rate (live)
panels.description: Tokens per second EACH active request is getting right now. Built from the decode-step counter, which advances while tokens are produced, times accepted MTP draft tokens per step when speculative decoding is on. The engine's token counters cannot be used for this: they only move when a request finishes, so a rate over them reads 0 for the whole of a long answer and spikes afterwards. 0 when idle -- it is never a stale value.

panels.title: Generation, finished requests (5 min)
panels.description: Average decode speed of requests that FINISHED in the last 5 minutes, as the engine timed them. Exact, but it only updates when a request completes. Shows 'idle' when nothing finished in the window, instead of carrying an old number forward.

panels.title: Prefill, finished requests (5 min)
panels.description: Prompt-processing speed of requests that finished in the last 5 minutes. 'idle' when none did.

panels.title: Active requests
panels.description: Requests being processed now, across all slots. The engine runs LLAMACPP_PARALLEL slots; beyond that, requests queue.

panels.title: Queued
panels.description: Requests waiting for a free slot. Anything above 0 for long means more concurrent users than slots.

panels.title: MTP draft acceptance (5 min)
panels.description: Share of multi-token-prediction draft tokens the model accepted, for requests finished in the last 5 minutes. Higher means more speedup. 'off' when speculative decoding is not enabled or nothing finished recently.

panels.title: Decode and prefill speed (tok/s)
panels.description: 'live decode' is per active request, right now. The two '(finished, 5 min)' lines are the engine's own timings of completed requests, so they lag and have gaps when nothing finished. None of these fall back to a lifetime average any more, which is what used to freeze the numbers.

panels.title: Token volume (per window)
panels.description: Tokens counted per window. The engine adds a request's tokens when it FINISHES, so a long answer appears as one bar at its end, not spread over the time it took.

panels.title: Prefix cache hit and MTP acceptance (%)
panels.description: Prefix cache hit: share of prompt tokens served from cache (a repeated system prompt or conversation history). MTP acceptance: share of draft tokens accepted. Both over finished requests, 5 min windows.

panels.title: Concurrency
panels.description: Requests in slots versus waiting for one. 'busy slots / decode' was removed: the engine exports it as a LIFETIME average, so it never reflected current load.

panels.title: GPU utilisation
panels.description: When the model's experts run on the CPU (--n-cpu-moe), expect LOW GPU% during generation: the GPU idles between attention layers. That is the design, not a fault.

panels.title: CPU utilisation (total)
panels.description: When the model's experts run on the CPU (--n-cpu-moe), this should be HIGH during generation: the expert matmuls run here. If tok/s is low and this is low too, the engine is waiting on memory or disk, not compute.

panels.title: CPU per core
panels.description: One line per logical CPU, however many the machine has: the seven busiest, and the rest as their average. Shows whether -t is actually spreading work, and whether some cores (on a hybrid CPU, the efficiency cores) are dragging.

panels.title: Memory: page cache is model residency
panels.description: The GGUF is mmap'd, so resident model weights show up as PAGE CACHE, not as used memory. Page cache collapsing means the model is being evicted and you will see tok/s fall with disk reads rising.

panels.title: Disk I/O — is the model paging?
panels.description: Per drive, as the machine names them. Sustained reads on the drive that holds the models DURING generation mean the working set does not fit and you are paging weights off disk. Brief reads at load are normal.

panels.title: Load average
panels.description: Above the logical CPUs line, runnable work is queuing for the CPU.

panels.title: CPU temperature
panels.description: The hottest CPU sensor and the average of all of them: two lines whatever the core count. The Resources dashboard has a line per sensor. Sustained CPU load can make the CPU throttle, which shows up as tok/s decay over a long run.

panels.title: NVMe temperature over time
panels.description: Each NVMe drive's composite temperature (SMART temp1) from node-exporter's hwmon collector, which reads the kernel's own nvme sensors -- node-exporter already mounts the host /sys, so no extra exporter is needed. A drive is named by its device, then the model it reports (node_nvme_info), as in nvme0 · <model>, or by its device alone when it reports no model. Some drives also report their NAND and controller as temp2/temp3, which the composite lags under sustained writes. SATA drives have no sensor here.

targets.expr: label_join(label_replace(node_hwmon_temp_celsius{chip=~"nvme_nvme[0-9]+",sensor="temp1"}, "device", "$1", "chip", "^nvme_(nvme[0-9]+)$") * on (instance, device) group_left (model) max by (instance, device, model) (node_nvme_info{model!=""}), "drive", " · ", "device", "model") or on (instance, chip) label_replace(node_hwmon_temp_celsius{chip=~"nvme_nvme[0-9]+",sensor="temp1"}, "drive", "$1", "chip", "^nvme_(nvme[0-9]+)$")

panels.title: Swap usage
panels.description: Swap being touched while the engine runs is a red flag: mmap'd model pages should be evicted from page cache instead. Growth here usually means something non-engine is under memory pressure.
